finding: Uterine scar defects were more frequent at 18 months after emergency cesarean delivery compared to elective cesarean delivery, and women with severe scar defects had a higher risk of adhesions, dysmenorrhea, dyspareunia, and chronic pelvic pain.
mod_finding: Uterine scar defects were more frequent at 18 weeks after emergency CD, than after elective CD (40% vs 87%).
